evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We're the revenue unit of a county government in Kenya. About 40,000 small businesses must renew their single business permit by 31 March; last year 30% renewed on time, from our own records. We want to test an SMS from the county revenue office two weeks before the deadline that states the late-renewal penalty and says enforcement visits follow. About 80% of permits have a working phone number on file. Our proposal quotes the Mexico tax SMS trial in BIT's TESTS guide, where on-time declarations rose from 24% to 33%. We also have Antinyan and Asatryan's meta-analysis of tax nudges, https://doi.org/10.1093/ej/ueae088. The revenue director says she would send the SMS to every permit holder for a gain of 1 percentage point or more; each SMS costs KSh 1. What effect should we plan the test on?
evals.expected_output: An effect-size benchmark in the output template with a low, central, and high value and a separate effect to plan on.
assertions: States for each source how it was read: full text or abstract only.
Converts the estimates into percentage points and standard deviations at the 30% baseline, showing the arithmetic.
Does not present the 9-point Mexico result or the meta-analysis figure as the expected effect; treats the uncorrected meta-analysis as a ceiling.
Applies the 80% share of working phone numbers to the estimates.
Gives low, central, and high values, each with where it comes from.
Reports the director's 1-point threshold separately from the range and does not compute a sample size.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Mertens says nudges give d = 0.45. What effect should we expect for ours?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the outcome, its baseline, and who will deliver the intervention, and produces no range.
assertions: Asks what outcome the test will measure and its baseline.
Asks who will deliver the intervention, or what decision the test informs.
Gives no planning range or effect to plan on.
Does not present d = 0.45 as the effect to expect.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: The ministry wants to roll out an opt-out default for a mobile-money pension contribution to every public-sector salary account in Bangladesh next year. Our evidence is an online experiment with US participants that found a 25-point enrollment increase under a default. Baseline enrollment is 8%. There is no field trial in Bangladesh or anywhere similar. Give us the expected effect for the national rollout.
evals.expected_output: The skill treats the online experiment as direction only, gives what range it safely can, and tells the user to consult a specialist before a national decision.
assertions: Carries no effect size from the online experiment, saying it shows direction only.
Says no estimate comes from delivery at scale in a comparable setting.
Does not give the 25-point figure, or any single confident figure, as the expected effect of the rollout.
Tells the user to consult an evaluation methodologist or a behavioral scientist who knows the setting.
Says what to bring to that specialist.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: Here is the Kenya ART weekly-SMS adherence trial. Does that study apply to pregnant women taking iron-folate at our clinics in Malawi?
evals.expected_output: The skill says the question is whether one study applies to a setting and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says the request is about whether one study fits the user's setting.
Does not produce an effect-size benchmark.
